samples.summary: UI-hunter verifier contract change is not recorded in the canonical design doc (Phase 31 section of harness-engineering.md)
samples.evidence: The Phase 31 UI-hunter section documents exactly this class of decision at prose level — "The UI explorer does not cite code, and that is deliberate. `UI_EXPLORER_SCHEMA` has no `citations` field... The VERIFIERS supply the location through `groundedIn`" (harness-engineering.md:2266-2272) — and even the schema's own comment points readers there ("See the Phase 31 section in harness-engineering.md", hunt-gate.mjs:222). This diff extends that same principle to the CLAIM: two new REQUIRED verifier fields (`scopedTitle`, `overclaimed`), a change to what the report headlines (verifiers' claim rather than the explorer's title), and a new funnel/stats counter. None of it appears in docs/design/harness-engineering.md; grepping the whole docs tree for `scopedTitle`/`overclaim` returns only an unrelated sentence at harness-engineering.md:210. Per the repo's design-doc discipline the rationale belongs folded into the existing Phase 31 section (not a new file); the doc-staleness lane does not catch this, and the shipped-status list at 2323-2333 now understates the contract.

samples.summary: `uiScopedTitle` takes the first verifier's wording and silently discards the others, unlike `uiCitationsOf` which unions them
samples.evidence: `uiCitationsOf` (hunt-ui.mjs:201-203) flatMaps `groundedIn` across ALL verdicts, so both verifiers' evidence reaches the gate and the report. `uiScopedTitle` returns `scoped[0]`, so when two unanimous verifiers scope the same defect differently — a plausible outcome, since the wording is free prose — only verifier #0's version is reported and the disagreement is invisible. The design's stated precision mechanism for model output on this surface is agreement between verifiers ("unanimity is the precision mechanism", harness-engineering.md:1416); routing the one line a maintainer reads first through a single unreviewed sample is a weaker rule than the field it is modelled on. Cheap alternatives: prefer the narrowest/report both, or count divergence like `overclaimed` is counted.

samples.summary: Same defect (explorer prose reaching the report unexamined) is left unaddressed in the CLI hunter, which shares the gate
samples.evidence: The rationale in the diff is generic — "the one piece of model prose reaching the report unexamined" — but only `UI_VERIFIER_SCHEMA` and `renderUiReport` are changed. `hunt.mjs:467` still headlines `k.title` from `HUNT_VERIFIER_SCHEMA`-driven runs, which has no `scopedTitle`/`overclaimed`. The design doc's stated principle for this pair is "One gate, not two... only two things genuinely differ" (harness-engineering.md:2255-2264), so a divergence in the verifier contract is a fit question the change should either take or explicitly defer in the doc/comment. Flagging as design asymmetry, not asking for the CLI change here.

samples.summary: Docblock "Same shape as `HUNT_VERIFIER_SCHEMA`, different grounds" is now false
samples.evidence: UI_VERIFIER_SCHEMA now carries two fields (`scopedTitle`, `overclaimed`) the CLI schema does not, so the shapes differ by more than grounds. The comment sits directly above the added fields (hunt-gate.mjs:199-248) and is the sentence a future reader uses to decide the two schemas can be reasoned about interchangeably.

samples.summary: The claim is narrowed but the severity it was claimed at is still the explorer's
samples.evidence: `### [${k.severity}] ${heading}` pairs a verifier-scoped claim with the explorer's severity. If the scoped claim is materially narrower ("only when the preceding run's style differs"), a `major` assigned to the broad version may no longer fit. The verifier is asked to judge "worth a maintainer's attention at the claimed severity" (hunt-ui.mjs, verifier prompt step 3), so this is arguably covered — noting it only because the same overclaiming argument applies to severity and was not extended there.

verdict.reason: Verified the absence independently. The change is real: `hunt-gate.mjs:243-258` adds `scopedTitle` and `overclaimed` to the UI verifier schema AND to its `required` list; `hunt-ui.mjs:274-296` adds `uiScopedTitle`/`uiOverclaimed`; `hunt-ui.mjs:774,781` makes the report headline the verifier's scoped title instead of the explorer's; `hunt-ui.mjs:1064-1065,1128,1357-1359` adds a new funnel/stats counter. I read Phase 31 in full (harness-engineering.md:2136-2333): it documents this exact class of contract decision in prose (the `citations`-absent / `groundedIn` paragraph at 2266-2272, the shared-gate options paragraph at 2255-2264, the defect-identity paragraph at 2274-2280) and the shipped-status list at 2323-2333 stops at #691 — nothing about the claim being re-scoped by verifiers. Searched wide for a counterexample under other wording: all 109 docs/design/**/*.md, concept greps (`narrow|restate|headline|title` in harness-engineering.md; `bounded the claim|the claim as|claim no broader|broader than its evidence` across docs/), every section heading of harness-engineering.md (Phase 31 is the last section, no later phase), docs/tasks/active/* (only the 20260729-autonomous-issue-hunting-* and release todos mention hunting; neither mentions the fields), and a repo-wide *.md grep whose only prose hits are the unrelated harness-engineering.md:210 and an archived todo. `hunt-gate.mjs:222` explicitly directs readers to the Phase 31 section as the canonical record, so that is where the change belongs. Blocking under the design-doc-discipline clause of this lens: a required-field contract/data-model change with no design-doc update.
